question.text: Find the slope of the tangent to the curve $y=\sqrt{3x^2+24}$ at the point where $x=-2.$
question.explanation:
To find the slope at a given point, we have to find $\dfrac {\textrm{d}y} {\textrm{d}x}$ at that point.

We use the chain rule in the form

\[ \dfrac{\textrm d y}{\textrm d x} = \dfrac{\textrm d y}{\textrm d u} \cdot \dfrac{\textrm d u}{\textrm d x}. \]

Let $u =3x^2+24.$ Then $y = \sqrt{u}.$ Differentiating, we have

\[ \dfrac{\textrm d y}{\textrm d u} = \dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{u}} \] and \[ \dfrac{\textrm d u}{\textrm d x} = 6x. \]

Multiplying the two together gives

\begin{align*} \dfrac{\textrm d y}{\textrm d x} &= \dfrac{\textrm d y}{\textrm d u} \cdot \dfrac{\textrm d u}{\textrm d x}\\[3pt] &= \dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{u}}\cdot 6x\\[3pt] &= \dfrac{3x}{\sqrt{3x^2+24}}. \end{align*}

Finally, substituting $x=-2,$ we get \[ \eqalign{ \left.\dfrac {\textrm{d}y} {\textrm{d}x}\right|_{x=-2} &=\left.\left(\dfrac{3x}{\sqrt{3x^2+24}}\right)\right|_{x=-2}\\ &=\dfrac{(-6)}{\sqrt{3(-2)^2+24}}\\ &=-\dfrac{6}{6} \\ &=-1\,. } \]

example.title: Differentiating a Radical Function Using the Chain Rule

question.explanation:
Let $g(x)=x^4-2x^3$ and $f(g(x)) = g(x)^{2}.$

Differentiating, we have \begin{align*} f'(g(x)) & = ( g^{2})' = 2g, \\ g'(x) & = (x^4-2x^3)' = 4x^3-6x^2. \end{align*}

Then, using the chain rule,

\begin{align*} f'(x) & = f'(g(x))\cdot g'(x)\\ & = 2g \cdot (4x^3-6x^2)\\ & = 2\left(x^4-2x^3\right )\left(4x^3-6x^2 \right). \end{align*}

example.title: Differentiating a Function Using the Chain Rule and Prime Notation

question.explanation:
Let $g(x)=x - x^2$ and $f(g(x)) = -\dfrac{4}{\sqrt{g}} = -4g^{-1/2}.$

Differentiating, we have \begin{align*} f'(g(x)) & = -4( g^{-1/2})' = 4\cdot \dfrac{1}{2} g^{-3/2} = \dfrac 2{g^{3/2}} , \\[5pt] g'(x) & = (x - x^2)' = 1 - 2x. \end{align*}

Then, using the chain rule,

\begin{align*} f'(x) & = f'(g(x))\cdot g'(x)\\[3pt] & = \dfrac{2}{g^{3/2}} \cdot (1 - 2x)\\[3pt] % & = \dfrac{2 - 4x}{g^{3/2} } \\[3pt] & = \dfrac{2 - 4x}{\sqrt{(x - x^2)^3} }. \end{align*}
